newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse buoyed by Gevaert deal.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse buoyed by Gevaert deal.

text.p: The Brussels bourse shrugged off bond market disappointment at preliminary French election results on Monday to push higher into record territory, helped by the latest news and speculation about mergers and alliances.

Early trade was dominated by the reaction to plans announced on Friday by holding companies Almanij and Cobepa to share out the assets of Gevaert. All three stocks surged in early dealings and analysts said the move put pressure on other holdings to simplify their structures too.
The Bel-20 index of 20 blue chips, none of which is directly concerned by Friday's news, hit a new record high.
Kredietbank was also firmer, adding another 1.6 percent (to 14,425 francs) to Friday's gain of 3.27 percent on news it was in exploratory alliance talks with Dutch Rabobank.

News of the Gevaert/Almanij/Cobepa deal also spilt over to some of Belgium's other holding companies, which make up more than half the listings in Brussels. Shares in Brederode, a market darling for months, had risen another 4.55 percent to 4,600 francs by midday. Brederode has made no secret that it too is considering simplifying its group structure, which includes five other listed holding companies.

The Bel-20's main gainer was Banque Bruxelles Lambert, up 4.42 percent at 9,450 francs as dealers refocused on the implications of Friday's main market rumour: that insurer Royale Belge might soon be sold to Dutch ING.

ING already owns 20 percent of BBL, the result of a failed 1992 takeover. If it bought Royale Belge it would immediately acquire another 12 percent of BBL and possibly more, as Royale Belge/BBL shareholder GBL, might also sell its stake.
Royale Belge was up just 30 francs, or 0.3 percent, to 9,950 francs, well off last week's highs ahead of the company's annual shareholders meeting on Wednesday.
